text.p: Western officials expressed concern on Monday that Bosnian opposition party members had been detained for alleged war crimes in breach of established procedure for such arrests.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), the body supervising Bosnia's first postwar elections, said 18 supporters of a separatist leader in northwest Bosnia had been arrested over the weekend.
Five of those arrested in Bihac and Velika Kladusa, once the stronghold of rebel warlord Fikret Abdic, had been detained for 30 days on war crimes charges. The rest had been released.
"The OSCE is concerned that the arrests appear to target members of the political opposition," OSCE spokesman David Foley told a news conference.

He said guidelines drawn up earlier this year as part of the Bosnian peace process specified that people could not be arrested for war crimes unless authorised by the International Criminal Tribunal for Yugoslavia (ICTY) in The Hague.
Foley said no case files on the arrested persons had been sent to the tribunal in The Hague.
"Files should be transferred immediately to the ICTY or these people should be released," Foley said.

Abdic, a Moslem businessman who led a separatist revolt during the war against Bosnian government forces in the Bihac enclave, is wanted by the Bosnian government for alleged war crimes. He now lives in Croatia.

In the run-up to Bosnian elections last month, Abdic ran a propaganda radio station in Croat-held territory in Bosnia. Bosnian authorities have in turn clamped down on Abdic sympathisers in the Bihac region.

United Nations officials meanwhile said that Bosnian Croat officials in the western town of Titov Drvar had prevented the return of 250 displaced Serbs, who had made the journey from Serb-held territory.
Croat officials halted the Serbs' five buses and a hostile crowd gathered. After a five-hour stand-off, the Bosnian Serbs returned to the town of Banja Luka.
